doc.title: Jack Sheldon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Working conditions on Merv's show
summary: An easy schedule, freedom to take off, substitutes, and comfort in front of cameras.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Merv Griffin was a pretty powerful man. Was he good to work for?
Yeah, great, really great. It was an easy job. We went in at 4:30 and we were through at 8:30. We’d work three days a week I think.
So you were filming a couple of shows a day or something?
Yeah. And he never bothered anybody. He let me do anything I wanted to do. He would cut it out if I got too weird, but that hardly ever happened though.
No, I can’t imagine. If you had a conflict, were you able to get your own substitute?

Yeah. We could always take off and do anything that happened. He didn’t like it if you took off too long, I think he got mad at Jake Hanna when he went with Supersax. And then Nick Ceroli started doing it.
But if you had to do a record date or anything — I was doing the series “The Girl With Something Extra” when I did Merv’s show. So I’d take off a lot during that.
Did it take a while to get comfortable in front of the cameras for you?

Not for me, no, I just loved it, you know I love it. And I feel better on the stage than I do anywhere else really, I’m more at home and more relaxed. It’s such fun for me, it really is fun, and the cameras being on makes it better. It’s exciting but mostly just fun.
